title: feat: add Mistral OCR 4
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds `mistral-ocr` with aliases `mistral-ocr-4` and `mistral-ocr-4-0` through existing `POST /v1/chat/completions` and `POST /text`; no separate Pollinations OCR endpoint or registry.
- Adapts one `file` or `image_url` to Mistral direct `/v1/ocr`, pinned to `mistral-ocr-4-0`; chat returns Markdown plus structured `ocr`/`content_blocks`, while `/text` returns Markdown.
- Contract: paid-only yes; multiplier 1; Mistral direct; Pollinations GPU no; fallback none. Streaming, prompt-only GET, and separately priced custom annotations are rejected.
- Bills exactly $0.004 per provider-reported processed page and bypasses text caching for document privacy and exact repeated billing.
- Review follow-up: keeps `upstreamRequestUrl` internal/non-enumerable, asserts the exact public response shape, and scopes OCR-only option validation to the canonical model and aliases so other text models retain passthrough behavior.
- Live E2E passed image and selected-page PDF through both text routes in 1.44s and 0.51s, each deducting 0.004 Pollen. Final verification: all 78 Gen files pass after the worktree dependency rerun, plus 310 Enter tests, SDK tests/build, Gen typecheck/staging build, and OpenAPI validation. No secret mutation.

Pricing: https://docs.mistral.ai/models/model-cards/ocr-4-0

gist.headline: Documents, meet the hive
gist.blurb: Mistral OCR 4 has joined the text routes, turning images and PDFs into useful Markdown without making anyone learn a new endpoint. Polli has been reading the paperwork. She remains politely unimpressed by it.
gist.summary: Added paid-only Mistral OCR 4 through POST /v1/chat/completions and POST /text, accepting one file or image_url and returning Markdown plus structured OCR content for chat requests.
gist.impact: Developers can extract text from images and selected-page PDFs using mistral-ocr, mistral-ocr-4, or mistral-ocr-4-0 on existing routes, billed at $0.004 Pollen per processed page with document responses kept out of the text cache.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy document-reading garden workshop: Polli helps a friendly CRT monitor robot convert a scanned PDF and an image into neatly sprouting Markdown code-plants. Page-shaped sheets, a magnifying glass, and small flowers represent OCR extraction, while a lime-green terminal shows the existing text API route rather than a separate OCR machine.
gist.image_prompt: Cozy pixel art scene in a warm garden workshop where the main character is a cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings; Polli wears tiny librarian glasses and gently holds a magnifying glass over a scanned PDF as Markdown code-plants sprout from its pages. A cute chunky CRT-monitor robot with eager square pixel eyes organizes an image and PDF beside a retro terminal glowing prominent lime green (#ecf874), with small flowers and vines around it; simple pixel-font terminal text reads “MISTRAL OCR 4”. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes, lo-fi Stardew Valley or A Short Hike feeling, nostalgic but beautiful.
